results.title: Higher Yields Prompt Banks to Boost SRBI Purchases Amid Slowing Credit Demand
results.body: Bank Indonesia raised the SRBI auction rate to 7.1%–8.65%, up from 4.78%–5.25% earlier in the year, making the instrument more attractive. As a result, banks now hold Rp 677.89 trillion of SRBI (69.18% of total outstanding), up from 62.03% a year earlier. Major banks highlighted their SRBI allocations: Bank Central Asia's securities holdings rose 17.54% YoY to Rp 425.41 trillion while its credit portfolio grew 4.54% YoY to Rp 965.01 trillion; CIMB Niaga's securities fell 1.57% YoY to Rp 75.62 trillion as its credit grew 6.99% YoY to Rp 171.39 trillion; OK Bank's securities rose 16.69% YoY to Rp 1.85 trillion as its credit expanded 6.26% YoY to Rp 10.12 trillion. Analysts note that banks with ample cheap liquidity are likely to continue parking funds in SRBI, while those with tighter liquidity may limit exposure amid competitive funding costs.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk continues its share buyback program with up to Rp5 trillion
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) received approval at its 2025 Annual General Meeting held on 12 March 2026 to continue its share buyback program. The buyback, authorized for a maximum of Rp5 trillion including transaction costs, will run for 12 months from 12 March 2026 to 11 March 2027, subject to earlier termination under applicable law. The company announced the continuation on 11 June 2026, stating the action reflects confidence in Indonesia’s capital market and its own fundamentals. BBCA’s shares closed up 3.10% (175 points) at 5,825 per share, on volume of 543.3 million shares and transaction value of Rp3.1 trillion.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announces continuation of share buyback program with up to Rp 5 trillion funding
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BCA) executed a share buyback on 11 June 2026, continuing the initiative first launched in April 2026. The program, approved at the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders for the 2025 fiscal year on 12 March 2026, is allocated a maximum of Rp 5 trillion to cover intermediary and related transaction costs. It is scheduled to run for 12 months, from 12 March 2026 to 11 March 2027, unless BCA terminates it earlier under applicable rules. President Director Hendra Lembong said the buyback reflects confidence in the Indonesian capital market and will not have a material impact on the bank’s financial condition or operations.
